myz_001: You can recognise it by its straight trunk with few heavy limbs, its crown visible from far off since nothing tall grows near it. It stands 400 metres off the highway, at the foot of a hill by the Oyodo river.
myz_004: You can recognise it as the wildest-looking of the akou figs, roots poured over the walls and rock. It stands to the right of the main hall at Nojima Shrine, on the Nichinan coast road.
myz_005: You can recognise it by its tall, needle-dropping conifer crown, unusual among the shrine's evergreens. It stands near the entrance to Miyazaki Shrine's main approach, on the left as you go in.
myz_006: You can recognise it by the stone marker set beneath it, with a ginkgo in front and an ogatama to its left. It stands to the right of the hall at Ikime Shrine.
myz_007: You can recognise it by its trunk, forking into two at about 1.8 metres up, on a low mound. It stands to the left of the worship hall at Sumiyoshi Hachiman Shrine.
myz_008: You can recognise it by its exposed roots, one carrying a knob rubbed smooth by hands over the years. It stands on the main approach at Eda Shrine, on the right as you face the worship hall.
